comparison: Perfect agreement on the core 'waterfall' finding (C3, C4, C56). Both evaluations rate this as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes analytical and simulation support from Figures 2-3, while peer reviewers explicitly call the evidence 'compelling' and note it as a 'major strength' with analytically solvable approximations.

Complete agreement on asymmetric accessibility (C5, C6). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites Figure 2a-c as direct support, while peer reviewers accept without challenge and explicitly affirm that 'small target frequencies can also be maintained' with appropriate initial conditions.

Strong agreement on multi-species extension (C9, C68-C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Figure 5 data and the distinction from hysteresis, while Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms the extension to three-species communities and generalizability of qualitative conclusions.

Agreement on main conclusions (C10, C78). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views these as well-supported by the entire analytical framework and simulation data, while peer reviewers affirm the practical implications and describe the study as 'important' with 'sobering message for designing concrete applications.'

Divergent evaluations on model assumptions (C27, C29-C32). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing transparent statement of assumptions as appropriate. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly noting limitations of exponential growth assumption and questioning generalizability to density-dependent demography.

Agreement on computational methodology (C79, C80, C82). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds the approach reasonable with appropriate citations, while Reviewer 3 explicitly praises the analytically solvable approximation as a 'major strength' and the editor affirms the mathematical analysis is 'compelling.'

Partial overlap on parameter effects. OpenEval R5 addresses C7 (N₀ effects) rated SUPPORTED, while peer R3 addresses C7, C8, C65 (both N₀ and g effects) rated UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers don't challenge technical correctness but Reviewer 2 questions practical interpretation, asking what N₀ means in experiments and noting 'the main result...cannot be taken advantage of by experimentalists' without clarification.

Partial overlap on growth rate parameter. OpenEval R6 addresses C8, C65 (g parameter effects) rated SUPPORTED with analytical justification. Peer R3 includes these claims with C7, rated UNCERTAIN due to practical interpretation concerns about experimental applicability rather than technical correctness.

Divergent evaluations on stochasticity scope (C41, C42). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing transparent statement of limitations as appropriate. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising substantive concern that the model focuses on demographic rather than environmental stochasticity, questioning whether this captures relevant experimental conditions.

Partial overlap on background context. OpenEval R1 addresses C1, C11-C13 (microbial collective capabilities), while peer R9 addresses broader background including C1, C2, C11-C26. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers treat these as accepted context and focus evaluation elsewhere, with Reviewer 1 affirming novelty relative to this background.

Partial overlap on background context. OpenEval R2 addresses C2, C14-C21 (challenges of collective selection), while peer R9 addresses broader background C1, C2, C11-C26. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes extensive prior work citations, while peer reviewers accept as framing context without detailed evaluation.

Partial overlap on prior work context. OpenEval R9 addresses C22-C26 (specific prior experimental work), while peer R9 addresses broader background C1, C2, C11-C26. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2 requests better explanation of structure-function relationships but doesn't challenge the claims themselves.

OpenEval evaluates C45, C52 (necessity of inter-collective selection and balance of forces) as SUPPORTED based on Appendix 1—figure 3b and Figure 2d. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval evaluates C57 (robustness to genotypes vs species distinction) as SUPPORTED based on Appendix 4 data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
